reason: No regulator requires agent-specific controls yet, and neither Robinhood nor Coinbase has shown me they run something like this, so I'm not going to be the design partner. The $1,500 isn't the issue; pushing a startup with no customers and no SOC 2 through vendor risk to sit in front of our MCP server is weeks of work for something nobody is asking us for.
objection: It isn't required. On top of that, I'd be the first customer of a vendor with no SOC 2. Shadow mode lowers the risk, but my security team still has to approve software inside our network, and I can't point to anyone bigger who has done it.
would_change_my_mind: FINRA putting out a notice or exam finding that expects specific controls on orders placed by AI agents, or seeing Robinhood or Coinbase put a gate like this in front of their agent trading.
